lessons.title: 1. Method Overloading
lessons.description: Java allows multiple methods with the same name if their parameter signatures differ. Implement two `multiply` methods: `multiply(int a, int b)` and `multiply(double a, double b)`.
learning_objectives: Overload methods with different parameter types in Java

tests.name: test_overloaded_multiply
tests.test_code: if (Solution.multiply(3, 4) != 12) throw new AssertionError("int multiply"); if (Math.abs(Solution.multiply(2.5, 2.0) - 5.0) > 0.001) throw new AssertionError("double multiply");

source.name: Oracle Java Tutorials — Overloading Methods — 'methods within a class can have the same name if they have different parameter lists'

lessons.title: 2. Helper Methods & Formatting
lessons.description: Break down problems into small private/public helper methods. Implement `formatName(String firstName, String lastName)` returning the last name, a comma and a space, then the first name.
learning_objectives: Format strings with String.format or concatenation in Java

tests.name: test_format_name
tests.test_code: if (!"Hopper, Grace".equals(Solution.formatName("Grace", "Hopper"))) throw new AssertionError("Expected Hopper, Grace");

source.name: Oracle Java Tutorials — Defining Methods
source.license: Oracle Free Use Terms and Conditions (documentation)

lessons.title: 3. Currency Exchange Calculator (Concept Challenge)

lessons.title: 4. String Sanitization (Practice)
lessons.description: Implement sanitize(String input): remove leading/trailing whitespace with trim() and convert to lowercase with toLowerCase() — return "" for null input. The test expects sanitize("  JAVA  ") to equal "java".
learning_objectives: Use String methods like trim() and toLowerCase()

tests.name: test_sanitize
tests.test_code: if (!"java".equals(Solution.sanitize("  JAVA  "))) throw new AssertionError("Expected java");

source.name: Java SE 21 API — String.trim() and String.toLowerCase()

lessons.title: 5. Unit 5 Checkpoint: Methods Mastery
lessons.description: Implement power(int base, int exponent) returning base raised to exponent as an int — e.g. Math.pow with an int cast, or a multiplying loop. The test expects power(2, 3) == 8.
